_comment: Hand-written. Seasons the league played that history.json carries no games for, because T.J.'s Yahoo account was not in them. Everything here was read off PUBLIC Yahoo profiles (profiles.sports.yahoo.com/profile/<handle>/fantasy, History tab) on 2026-11-17 - no logins, no league access. Placements only: no win-loss, points, or matchups exist for these years yet. seasons.py never writes this file. Working: _shared/yahoo_league_record.md. The help block asks only for Standings and Draft Results on purpose: those two pages carry no email addresses, unlike the Teams page. No email address appears here either - the site is public and the repo is public.

help.heading: Were you in this season? You can fill it in
help.intro: If this year is still on your Yahoo account, you can hand over the whole season in about two minutes. Nothing technical, and no screenshots needed.
steps: Sign in to Yahoo Fantasy Football.
Go to football.fantasysports.yahoo.com/YEAR/f1/myleagues, swapping YEAR for the year above, and click the league. The number in the address bar is its league ID, and that alone is worth sending.
Open the Standings page, press Ctrl+S (Cmd+S on a Mac) and choose "Webpage, HTML Only". Save it anywhere.
Do the same on the Draft Results page.
Email T.J. those two files and the league ID.
help.why: Those two pages hold the final standings, every record and the whole draft board. Neither contains an email address, so nothing private leaves your account.
help.commish: If you were the commissioner that year, check first whether your commissioner tools still let you set the league to publicly viewable. If they do, flipping that one switch saves you every step above.
help.fallback: Cannot save the pages? Select all on the Standings page, copy, and paste it into the email instead. The numbers survive as text, which is all that is needed.

2009.most_wanted: Five of the ten places are still blank, and so is every score and the entire draft. Any of it helps.

possible.note: finished 5th or 6th - he played three 10-team leagues in 2009, so which one was FL Players is not pinned down

prose: The league played 2009, and for years the site could not show it. T.J. was not in it - his only football league that season was an eight-team side league called crazy wacky action bike - so none of 2009 reached the archive through his account.

It is back in view now, not from league data but from the managers themselves. A Yahoo profile is public, and it lists every league that account ever played with the team count and where they finished. Line those up across the managers and the season reassembles.
Ten teams. Brett won it. J Rock was second and Austin third, and DJ finished ninth. Five places are still blank, and so is every score, every matchup and the whole draft.

2011.most_wanted: One answer matters more than everything else here: who won 2011. If you know, that alone closes the oldest open question on this site.

possible.note: finished 7th or 8th - he played two 10-team leagues in 2011

prose: 2011 is the one season nobody on the site can name a champion for. The league played it, ten teams, and T.J. was away - his Yahoo account holds no football league at all that year.
Four places are known, read off public profiles: Austin second, Brett third, DJ fourth, J Rock sixth. Tyler was seventh or eighth.

The winner is the gap. Every manager whose profile can be read has been checked, and not one of them finished first - so 2011 was won by an account whose teams are hidden on Yahoo, which is how several teams from that era appear. Someone in the league knows who it was.
